newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel says summit with Egypt will go ahead.
newsitem.headline: Israel says summit with Egypt will go ahead.

text.p: Israel said on Sunday a summit between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak would go ahead as planned.

"The summit will take place on Tuesday," Cabinet Secretary Danny Naveh told Israel Television after talks in Jerusalem with an Egyptian envoy sent to prepare the ground for the summit at Egypt's Red Sea resort of Sharm el-Sheikh.
"It will be a first step towards narrowing the gap between the sides, between us and the Palestinians," Naveh said.
Israel's Yedioth Ahronoth daily had said the summit was in danger of being cancelled because of Israel's refusal to agree ahead of time to stop building a Jewish settlement in East Jerusalem.
The PLO has demanded Israel scrap the project as a condition for resuming peace talks suspended since the Netanyahu government broke ground at the site on March 18.

Before Naveh's announcement, Netanyahu told Israel Army Radio that stopping work at the hilltop Israel calls Har Homa and Palestinians refer to as Jabal Abu Ghneim would not be on his agenda for the summit. Naveh gave no indication the position had changed.
